gp.text: The Company uses certain operating performance measures, specifically consolidated gross margin, operating margin by segment and consolidated operating margin, to manage the Company's businesses, set operational goals, and establish performance targets for incentive compensation for the Company's employees. The Company defines consolidated gross margin as a percentage of total consolidated gross profit to total consolidated net sales. The Company defines operating margin by segment as a percentage of total income from operations by segment to total net sales by segment and consolidated operating margin as a percentage of total consolidated income from operations to total consolidated net sales. The Company believes consolidated gross margin, consolidated operating margin, and operating margin by segment may be useful to investors in evaluating the profitability of the Company's segments and the Company on a consolidated basis.

Residential.text: On December 17, 2024, the Company sold its electronic locker business within its Residential segment to a third party and received net proceeds of $28 million.

Agtech.text: Net sales in the Company's Agtech segment increased 32.4%, or $11.0 million, to $45.0 million for the three months ended March 31, 2025 compared to $34.0 million for the three months ended March 31, 2024. The revenue increase was largely due to $15.3 million generated from the current quarter acquisition of Lane Supply, which more than offset a 12.6% decrease in organic sales related to project start delays for two produce projects waiting on permit approval. The Company expects to have permits finalized and start construction around the end of the second quarter. Backlog increased 226% year over year in this segment, driven by both organic orders and with the acquisition of Lane Supply.

Infrastructure.heading: • Infrastructure
Infrastructure.text:
The Company serves customers primarily in North America including home improvement retailers, wholesalers, distributors, contractors, institutional and commercial growers of fruits, vegetables, flowers and other plants, convenience store, travel centers, food retailers, and quick-serve restaurants, and renewable energy (solar) developers.

At March 31, 2025, the Company operated forty facilities, comprised of thirty-two manufacturing facilities, two distribution centers, and six offices, which are located in nineteen states, Canada, and China. The Company's operational infrastructure provides the necessary scale to support local, regional, and national customers in each of the Company's markets.

gp.text: The Company uses certain operating performance measures, specifically consolidated gross margin, operating margin by segment and consolidated operating margin, to manage the Company's businesses, set operational goals, and establish performance targets for incentive compensation for the Company's employees. The Company defines consolidated gross margin as a percentage of total consolidated gross profit to total consolidated net sales. The Company defines operating margin by segment as a percentage of total income from operations by segment to total net sales by segment and consolidated operating margin as a percentage of total consolidated income from operations to total consolidated net sales. The Company believes consolidated gross margin, consolidated operating margin, and operating margin by segment may be useful to investors in evaluating the profitability of the Company's segments and the Company on a consolidated basis.

tax.text: The Company recognized a provision for income taxes of $9.8 million, with an effective tax rate of 32.3% for the three months ended September 30, 2026. The effective tax rate for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was greater than the U.S. federal statutory rate of 21% due to state taxes and nondeductible permanent differences partially offset by benefits related to tax credit generation or utilization. The Company recognized a provision for income taxes of $8.7 million, with an effective tax rate of 20.8% for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The effective tax rate for the three months ended September 30, 2025 was less than the U.S. federal statutory rate of 21% due to favorable discrete items related to an excess tax benefit on stock-based compensation and the benefit of purchased tax credits that will be carried back to prior tax years.

Residential.text: On February 2, 2026, the Company acquired OmniMax, a leading U.S.- and Canada-based manufacturer and provider of residential roofing accessories and rainwater management systems. The acquisition of OmniMax furthers the Company's goal of helping innovate and reshape the markets in which it operates and provide better solutions for its customers and the channels it serves.

Agtech.text: The Company believes that the planned sale of DSB represents an important step in the continued simplification of its portfolio and further sharpens its strategic focus and resource allocation toward its Residential and Agtech segments. Subject to completion of the transaction, the Company currently expects the transaction to be highly tax-efficient, which is anticipated to maximize net proceeds available to support debt reduction and strengthen the Company's balance sheet. The transaction remains subject to customary closing conditions, and there can be no assurance that the transaction will be completed on the currently contemplated terms or timeframe.

Infrastructure.text: On October 14, 2026, the Company entered into an agreement to sell its Infrastructure business. The sale furthers the simplification of the Company's portfolio and sharpens its strategic focus and resource allocation on its Residential and Agtech segments.

lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately

s.t: One customer, a home improvement retailer which purchases from the Residential segment, represented 12%, 16% and 17% of the Company's consolidated net sales for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively.
No other customer in any segment or segments accounted for more than 10% of the Company's consolidated net sales.

In 2025, approximately 70% of the Company's revenues were generated from sales to retailers, wholesalers and distributors and approximately 30% from products and services that were sold directly to contractors or the end users.

The Company's ten largest customers accounted for approximately 43%, 42%, and 46% of the Company's net sales during 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively, with its largest customer accounting for approximately 12%, 16% and 17% of the Company's consolidated net sales during each of the years 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively.

Demand for products in the Company’s Residential segment depends on the level of residential improvement and renovation and new construction activity, and, in particular, the amount of spending on home exteriors and living spaces.

The success of the Company's business depends on the Company's senior management team, as well as other key employees and the Company's ability to attract, retain, develop and motivate a skilled and diverse workforce.
If the subcontractors the Company relies upon do not perform their contractual obligations, the Company's business, results of operations and cash flows would be adversely affected.
The Company depends on the quality and timeliness of work performed by its subcontractors.
The Company's ability to effectively manage its business depends on the security, reliability, and capacity of these IT systems.

The Company’s ability to make scheduled payments of the principal of, to pay interest on, and to refinance its debt, depends on its future performance, which is subject to economic, financial, competitive and other factors.
The Company’s ability to refinance its outstanding indebtedness or future indebtedness will depend on the capital markets and its financial condition at such time.

The impact to the Company's operating results would significantly depend on the competitive environment and the costs of other alternative products, which could impact the Company's ability to pass commodity costs to customers.
The Company is exposed to foreign exchange risk as a result of the Company's international operations, primarily in Canada, and through sales to and purchases from foreign customers and vendors.
